title: Stonebridge
thesis: Your first full round here was 103 on Jul 11, about seven under your usual 110, and the front has since dropped to 46. Bring the whole plan to all 18. This is a water course: nearly every hole has a way to make a big number, and every one is optional. One dry ball, aim centre, advance to a wedge, take the bogey.

tempo.label: Your one swing thought, every club
tempo.note: Full and committed, never light. If smooth won't reach, club up. "More" is the miss.

keys: Smooth is full and committed, not light. Every green you have hit in regulation came from a committed smooth swing. Light and steery is where the topped and the short ones come from. Commit to the club.

"More" is the miss. Three times last round, reaching for extra turned into a slice right and LOST distance. If smooth will not get there, club up. Never swing harder. This is your most reliable finding.

Aim the dry side, one ball in play. Water is on 1, 3, 5 up front and 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18 on the back. Aim away from it every time and never re-tee into it. A dry double beats a wet triple, every hole.
New watch: play the centre number, then club up. Take the front/centre/back reading, use centre, and add a club. You come up short, so the honest number is longer than it feels. Centre plus one.
Short game and putt speed win the card. Chipping is your strength, so lean on it after every missed green. On the greens, die it at the hole. Speed is your only miss; the lines are already good.
